notes.text: Baseline panel. Blood draw on cycle day 10 (late follicular). Ferritin already borderline low — doctor recommended iron supplementation. Feeling fatigued, especially around periods.

Late-follicular draw on cycle day 11. Estradiol was rising while progesterone remained low, consistent with the recorded cycle. Ferritin dropped further despite 25 mg iron, so she switched to iron bisglycinate 36 mg with vitamin C. TSH is creeping up and will be monitored.

Late-luteal draw on cycle day 27, three days before the next recorded period. Hemoglobin, ferritin, and transferrin saturation all improved on a consistent 36 mg iron-bisglycinate dose. TSH continues to rise while free T4 trends down, so the GP ordered thyroid antibodies.

Cycle day 10 (late follicular). Ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hemoglobin continue to improve after sustained adherence to iron bisglycinate. TSH is still rising and free T4 is near the lower boundary, so thyroid antibodies and an endocrinology review remain pending.

assessments.interpretation:
## The bedroom is comparatively well controlled

- Bedroom RF measured 8.5 µW/m² and AC magnetic field measured 25 nT, both lower than the street-facing living room in this assessment. The 3.2 V/m AC electric reading is the main bedroom item to recheck after moving the meter and changing breaker states.
- Existing night routines — WiFi off and phone in airplane mode — should be kept consistent before and during any repeat measurement.
- The living room has the highest measured RF at 180 µW/m², consistent with the street-facing windows, nearby networks, and reported cell-tower line of sight. Distance from the windows and relocating the router are practical comparison tests.

No office was measured, and phone exposure was not measured separately, so neither should be treated as a confirmed finding from this assessment.

focusCard.text: Ferritin is 42 µg/L in July 2026, up from 24 in August 2025 after sustained iron-bisglycinate use but still below the personal 50+ goal. Hemoglobin improved from 126 to 138 g/L and transferrin saturation from 16% to 28%, so the iron markers tell a consistent recovery story. The draw was cycle day 10. TSH has risen to 3.8 mIU/L while free T4 has declined to 12.5 pmol/L; both remain within the fixture's displayed ranges, but the trend and maternal Hashimoto's history support completing TPOAb and TgAb testing before labeling or treating thyroid disease.
